chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Suleyman ibn Salih who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the lowest degree of what comes from the limit of extravagance?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Your devaluing your kept garment, and pouring out the excess from your vessel, and you eating the dates and throwing the pits here and there.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum level of extravagance according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the minimum threshold of extravagance (israf) through everyday actions, such as discarding usable clothing, wasting food or drink, and carelessly discarding date pits. This highlights that extravagance is not limited to excess spending but includes wastefulness in the use of ordinary possessions. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith establishes the principle of *israf* as a violation of the trust (*amanah*) placed in humans to utilize God's blessings with moderation, extending the concept beyond mere financial waste to include the physical disposal of resources.
